column1: # The red run: this tree's assertions against the engine the base ref holds,
# written whole by tests/red, which tests/run --record-assertions calls.
#   base  <ref>  <sha>  <engine version there>
#   run   <failed>  <passed>  <skipped>        lines counted, not the summary
#   <assertion name>  <times it failed>        failed names only
#   an assertion the manifest lists that the base run never reached counts as failed, by its shortfall
# A base of - means no complete red run was made: none was possible, the
# suite stopped before reached or reached no assertion, or tests/red itself
# was stopped; its stdout said which unless it was the one stopped.
# Reproduce with: tests/red <ref>
base
run
D1: a FELIX_TEST_JOBS the caller already had is replaced by the core count
D1: only the value true stops it: GITHUB_ACTIONS=false still sets the core count
D1: the core count is held to 64 (sysctl 200, getconf 100), falls from sysctl to getconf to 1, and sysctl answers first and a non-number does not
D1: when tests/run exits 2 with one line on stderr the gate reports tests FAIL and shows the log's last line under it
D1: when tests/run exits 2, the log's last line is shown under tests FAIL
D1: with GITHUB_ACTIONS unset gate.sh sets FELIX_TEST_JOBS to the core count for its call to tests/run, and its argument list stays --reuse
D1: with GITHUB_ACTIONS unset, gate.sh sets FELIX_TEST_JOBS to the core count for its call to tests/run (sysctl, then getconf, then 1; held to 1 to 64)
D4: a unit that dies in red's suite only: the record run exits 0, no process is left, and red.tsv counts the run with name rows that add up to its failed count
D4: a unit that prints reached in red's suite only makes red refuse the log, the record run having passed: red.tsv holds the rows base - - - and run - - -
D4: and no name row starts with one of the runner's seven failure prefixes, and djx b2, which the dead unit never reached, is named by its shortfall of one
D4: and over a base that has one and a tree that has none, red removes the base's: its -j suite refuses, and red.tsv holds the rows base - - - and run - - -
D4: red's suite ran its three units as three separate processes, which a serial suite does not (FELIX_TEST_RED_JOBS)
R10: and with GITHUB_ACTIONS=true and a FELIX_TEST_JOBS=7 it inherited, the stub sees it unset
R10: and with a valid FELIX_TEST_RED_JOBS=2 its suite runs -j 2: the three parts ran in three processes, whatever FELIX_TEST_JOBS says
R10: red by hand with FELIX_TEST_JOBS=3 runs its suite serially: one process ran the three parts, and red.tsv counts

R10: with GITHUB_ACTIONS=true and a FELIX_TEST_JOBS=7 the caller already had, the stub sees it unset, and the argument list is --reuse

R32: a TERM sent to red's monitor between its STOP and its KILL, while it stops a suite whose unit ignores TERM (the suite's own ending held, so it stops nothing first, as red's suite is a fork on bash 3.2 and the -j parent itself on 5.2), changes nothing: the record run exits within 45 s of the sleeper's start, not after the 60 s it gives red, and the TERM landed with processes stopped
R32: and red.tsv holds the rows base - - - and run - - -, the manifest is as it was, and nothing of the group is left, stopped or running
